Hanf.et:
From Middle High German hanef, hanif, hanf, from Old High German hanaf, from Proto-West Germanic *hanapi, from Proto-Germanic *hanapiz.

Hänfling.et:
Hanf + -ling
The bird was so called for its fondness for hemp seeds (cf. English linnet). The colloquial usage for a person is by comparison to a hemp plant (cf. English beanpole).

hanfen.et: From Middle High German henfīn, henepfīn, from Old High German hanafīn, from Proto-West Germanic *hanapīn, equivalent to Hanf + -en. Cognate with German Low German hempen, Dutch hennepen, English hempen.

s: any plant of the genus Trachycarpus, a taxonomic genus within the family Arecaceae, comprising eleven species of fan palms (subfamily Coryphoideae) native to Asia
